legalName: Petition for Expungement of Police and Court Records of a Non-Conviction, Va. Code § 19.2-392.2(A)
publicName: Expunge a Virginia charge that did not end in a conviction
mechanism: Read at source on 2026-08-06 in the version effective until December 1, 2026, § 19.2-392.2(A) allows a person charged with a crime, a civil offence or any offence defined in Title 18.2 who is acquitted, or against whom a nolle prosequi is taken or the charge is otherwise dismissed including dismissal by accord and satisfaction under § 19.2-151, to petition for expungement of the police and court records relating to the charge, and provides that no court fees or costs are payable. Subsection C fixes venue in the circuit court of the county or city where the case was disposed of, prescribes the petition contents, and requires the petitioner to request that the CCRE electronically forward a copy of the petitioner's Virginia criminal history record to that court. Subsection D gives the attorney for the Commonwealth twenty-one days to object, answer or give written notice of no objection. Subsection F applies the manifest injustice standard but adds a presumption the controlling review could not verify: where the petitioner has no prior criminal record and the arrest was for a misdemeanor violation or the charge was a civil offence, the petitioner is entitled to expungement in the absence of good cause shown to the contrary by the Commonwealth. Subsection F also allows the court to enter the order without a hearing where the Commonwealth gives written notice of no objection and, for a felony charge, stipulates manifest injustice. Subsection K makes State Police validate the accuracy of the record but not its eligibility. Subsection L makes an order voidable within three years. Subsection M keeps the petition and any responsive pleadings under seal.
exclusions: A charge dismissed after a finding of facts sufficient for guilt, and a deferred or first-offender disposition such as a § 18.2-251 drug dismissal. Under Commonwealth v. Dotson 'otherwise dismissed' is read narrowly and this population routes to sealing instead.
Convictions, other than those reached by the pardon and actual-innocence subsections, which are their own tracks.
Records where another person used the petitioner's identity, which is § 19.2-392.2(B) and a different track with a fingerprint requirement.
Juvenile records, which are a separate regime.
Federal records; Virginia relief reaches Virginia records only.

waitingPeriods.duration: None. Section 19.2-392.2 imposes no waiting period.

venue: The circuit court of the county or city in which the case was disposed of by acquittal or by being otherwise dismissed. District court charges are filed in that locality's circuit court.

destination.name: Clerk of the circuit court of the locality where the case was disposed of
destination.detail: File the petition with a copy of the warrant, summons or indictment if reasonably available. No court fees or costs are payable. Serve a copy on the attorney for the Commonwealth of that locality, who has twenty-one days to respond. Separately request that the CCRE forward the criminal history record electronically to the court.

participantActionRequired.description: Obtain The participant's own Virginia criminal history record from the CCRE. Request your own copy from the CCRE for the fee they charge. This is a different thing from the court's copy: you must separately ask the CCRE to forward a copy electronically to the circuit court as part of the petition. The Norfolk clerk's guidance is that the case is established with the court first and the State Police request comes second, so the sequence matters.

releaseBlockers.question: Chapter 23.2 and § 19.2-392.2 both carry future versions that the controlling review predates and does not record. Read at source on 2026-08-06: § 19.2-392.2 exists in two versions, one effective until December 1, 2026 and one effective December 1, 2026, the later of which broadens subsection A to any person 'arrested, charged, summonsed, or indicted' who 'is not ultimately convicted' provided no stipulation or judicial finding of facts sufficient to find guilt and no deferred adjudication, codifies the Dotson limit in the statute itself, and adds a new subsection C sentence permitting a single petition to cover multiple charges arising out of SEPARATE transactions or occurrences. Section 19.2-392.6 likewise carries an A subsection effective until July 1, 2027 and a second effective July 1, 2027, and its historical citation now includes 2026, Sp. Sess. I, c. 1, which the review did not have. The review's open question about a 2026 amendment is therefore answered in the affirmative. Every Virginia track must be re-read before 2026-12-01 and again before 2027-07-01.

provenance.sourceStatement: Is there a 2026 session amendment to Chapter 23.2? A search result rendering of section 19.2-392.12:1 displayed subsection A as "(Effective until July 1, 2027)," which would imply a 2026 act creating a later version. The section page read at source on this date shows only the 2025 chapters 634 and 671 in its historical citation and no dual version. **Nonblocking research note with a standing monitor**, and it should be resolved before the next Virginia refresh.
provenance.counselQuestion: 2026 Sp. Sess. I, c. 1 creates a July 1, 2027 version of § 19.2-392.6(A), and § 19.2-392.2 has a version effective December 1, 2026 that broadens the expungement gateway and codifies Dotson. Which version does the packet build against between now and 1 December 2026, and what is the cutover plan?

releaseBlockers.question: What the December 1, 2026 version of § 19.2-392.2 does to this track. Read at source on 2026-08-06, the later version replaces the subsection A gateway with any person 'arrested, charged, summonsed, or indicted' for an infraction, crime or civil offence who 'is not ultimately convicted, provided that no stipulation of facts sufficient to find guilt was entered or the court did not determine the facts sufficient to find guilt but deferred adjudication or disposition to a later date'. That codifies the Dotson limit in the statute, extends the route to infractions, and adds a sentence to subsection C permitting a single petition to cover multiple charges arising out of separate transactions or occurrences, which the current version does not allow. It also provides that unavailability of the arrest information alone is not a basis for refusing expungement, and requires an objecting Commonwealth's Attorney to state the basis. The packet must be rebuilt for that version before it takes effect.
